previous_description: Distinct state that the experience can be in (works across all channels)
definition: A named, mutually exclusive condition of a user experience's state machine (e.g. idle, loading, editing, submitted, error) that fixes which components are enabled, disabled or hidden while it is active and owns the entry/exit actions and outgoing transitions for that condition. It is a node in the machine, not a screen, route or event.

distinguish_from.when: the thing is a reusable template made of several named states and their transitions (e.g. 'wizard', 'optimistic-update'), rather than one state within a machine
the thing is the event-driven edge that moves the experience from one state to another, with a trigger, guard and destination
the thing is a routable screen, modal or panel with its own URL or display mode; a state is a condition within or across views, not the container being shown
the thing is a side effect (focus, scroll, dispatch, navigate) executed on entering, exiting or transitioning out of a state, not the state itself

standard_reference: W3C SCXML 1.0 §3.3 <state> element (no direct HTML 5.3 equivalent; component effects map to ARIA aria-disabled/aria-hidden)
code_evidence: a key under 'states' in an XState/Robot/Zag machine config (e.g. states: { loading: { entry: ..., on: { SUCCESS: 'done' } } }) or a state class in a State-pattern implementation
a member of a status union or enum (e.g. type Status = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'error') held in useState, useReducer, a Redux/Pinia store or component data and switched on in render logic
conditional rendering or prop toggles keyed on that status value, such as `if (status === 'error') return <ErrorPanel/>` or `disabled={status === 'submitting'}` or `hidden={state.matches('editing')}`

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of what condition this state represents and what the user sees or can do while it is active; set it whenever the state name alone does not make the condition clear.

notes: channel duplicates UXSpec.experience with a different enum (web/mobile vs visual). No final/terminal flag or parent-state attribute for hierarchical statecharts. Outgoing associated-with, governs and renders to ux.view overlap; pick one. 'specializes' to statepattern is semantically wrong (state is a member, not a subtype); chartseries 'uses' experiencestate looks spurious.
